author: Emily Dickinson
handle: I heard a fly buzz when I died
text: I heard a fly buzz when I died; The stillness round my form Was like the stillness in the air Between the heaves of storm.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Success is counted sweetest
text: Success is counted sweetest By those who ne'er succeed. To comprehend a nectar Requires sorest need.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Our share of night to bear
text: Our share of night to bear, Our share of morning, Our blank in bliss to fill, Our blank in scorning.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: 'T is so much joy! 'T is so much joy!
text: 'T is so much joy! 'T is so much joy! If I should fail, what poverty! And yet, as poor as I Have ventured all upon a throw;

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Glee! The great storm is over!
text: Glee! The great storm is over! Four have recovered the land; Forty gone down together Into the boiling sand.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Some things that fly there be,
text: Some things that fly there be, -- Birds, hours, the bumble-bee: Of these no elegy. Some things that stay there be, --

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: When night is almost done
text: When night is almost done, And sunrise grows so near That we can touch the spaces, It 's time to smooth the hair

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Read, sweet, how others strove
text: Read, sweet, how others strove, Till we are stouter; What they renounced, Till we are less afraid;

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Pain has an element of blank
text: Pain has an element of blank; It cannot recollect When it began, or if there were A day when it was not.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: I taste a liquor never brewed
text: I taste a liquor never brewed, From tankards scooped in pearl; Not all the vats upon the Rhine Yield such an alcohol!

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: 'T was such a little, little boat
text: 'T was such a little, little boat That toddled down the bay! 'T was such a gallant, gallant sea That beckoned it away!

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Whether my bark went down at sea
text: Whether my bark went down at sea, Whether she met with gales, Whether to isles enchanted She bent her docile sails;

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: The brain within its groove
text: The brain within its groove Runs evenly and true; But let a splinter swerve, 'T were easier for you

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Mine by the right of the white election!
text: Mine by the right of the white election! Mine by the royal seal! Mine by the sign in the scarlet prison Bars cannot conceal!

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: You left me, sweet, two legacies,
text: You left me, sweet, two legacies, -- A legacy of love A Heavenly Father would content, Had He the offer of;

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Alter? When the hills do
text: Alter? When the hills do. Falter? When the sun Question if his glory Be the perfect one.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Doubt me, my dim companion!
text: Doubt me, my dim companion! Why, God would be content With but a fraction of the love Poured thee without a stint.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: If you were coming in the fall
text: If you were coming in the fall, I'd brush the summer by With half a smile and half a spurn, As housewives do a fly.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: I hide myself within my flower
text: I hide myself within my flower, That wearing on your breast, You, unsuspecting, wear me too -- And angels know the rest.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Have you got a brook in your little heart
text: Have you got a brook in your little heart, Where bashful flowers blow, And blushing birds go down to drink, And shadows tremble so?

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: As if some little Arctic flower
text: As if some little Arctic flower, Upon the polar hem, Went wandering down the latitudes, Until it puzzled came

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: My river runs to thee
text: My river runs to thee: Blue sea, wilt welcome me? My river waits reply. Oh sea, look graciously!

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: 'T was a long parting, but the time
text: 'T was a long parting, but the time For interview had come; Before the judgment-seat of God, The last and second time

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: She rose to his requirement, dropped
text: She rose to his requirement, dropped The playthings of her life To take the honorable work Of woman and of wife.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Come slowly, Eden!
text: Come slowly, Eden! Lips unused to thee, Bashful, sip thy jasmines, As the fainting bee,

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Perhaps you'd like to buy a flower?
text: Perhaps you'd like to buy a flower? But I could never sell. If you would like to borrow Until the daffodil

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: The grass so little has to do,
text: The grass so little has to do, -- A sphere of simple green, With only butterflies to brood, And bees to entertain,

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: A drop fell on the apple tree
text: A drop fell on the apple tree, Another on the roof; A half a dozen kissed the eaves, And made the gables laugh.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: This is the land the sunset washes
text: This is the land the sunset washes, These are the banks of the Yellow Sea; Where it rose, or whither it rushes, These are the western mystery!

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Like trains of cars on tracks of plush
text: Like trains of cars on tracks of plush I hear the level bee: A jar across the flowers goes, Their velvet masonry

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Presentiment is that long shadow on the lawn
text: Presentiment is that long shadow on the lawn Indicative that suns go down; The notice to the startled grass That darkness is about to pass.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: As children bid the guest good-night
text: As children bid the guest good-night, And then reluctant turn, My flowers raise their pretty lips, Then put their nightgowns on.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Angels in the early morning
text: Angels in the early morning May be seen the dews among, Stooping, plucking, smiling, flying: Do the buds to them belong?

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: It makes no difference abroad
text: It makes no difference abroad, The seasons fit the same, The mornings blossom into noons, And split their pods of flame.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: The mountain sat upon the plain
text: The mountain sat upon the plain In his eternal chair, His observation omnifold, His inquest everywhere.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: I'll tell you how the sun rose,
text: I'll tell you how the sun rose, -- A ribbon at a time. The steeples swam in amethyst, The news like squirrels ran.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Apparently with no surprise
text: Apparently with no surprise To any happy flower, The frost beheads it at its play In accidental power.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: These are the days when birds come back
text: These are the days when birds come back, A very few, a bird or two, To take a backward look. These are the days when skies put on

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: The sky is low, the clouds are mean
text: The sky is low, the clouds are mean, A travelling flake of snow Across a barn or through a rut Debates if it will go.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: I think the hemlock likes to stand
text: I think the hemlock likes to stand Upon a marge of snow; It suits his own austerity, And satisfies an awe

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: There's a certain slant of light
text: There's a certain slant of light, On winter afternoons, That oppresses, like the weight Of cathedral tunes.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Safe in their alabaster chambers
text: Safe in their alabaster chambers, Untouched by morning and untouched by noon, Sleep the meek members of the resurrection, Rafter of satin, and roof of stone.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: On this long storm the rainbow rose
text: On this long storm the rainbow rose, On this late morn the sun; The clouds, like listless elephants, Horizons straggled down.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: My cocoon tightens, colors tease
text: My cocoon tightens, colors tease, I'm feeling for the air; A dim capacity for wings Degrades the dress I wear.

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Exultation is the going
text: Exultation is the going Of an inland soul to sea, -- Past the houses, past the headlands, Into deep eternity!

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: Look back on time with kindly eyes
text: Look back on time with kindly eyes, He doubtless did his best; How softly sinks his trembling sun In human nature's west!

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: A train went through a burial gate
text: A train went through a burial gate, A bird broke forth and sang, And trilled, and quivered, and shook his throat Till all the churchyard rang;

author: Emily Dickinson
handle: I died for beauty, but was scarce
text: I died for beauty, but was scarce Adjusted in the tomb, When one who died for truth was lain In an adjoining room.
